sections.title: arXiv AI daily — announcement batch 2026-11-22 | 8 papers
sections.summary: This batch spans agent behavior, efficient formal instruction translation, VLM privacy and memory, and evaluation for clinical audio and multilingual vision-language models. Spoken agenda: agent systems, efficiency and safety evidence, and open evaluation gaps.

sections.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective
sections.abstract: The paper models agent states and a statistical-mechanical potential to track how post-training organizes LLM-agent behavior, demonstrating the measures on safety-test selection and physics-reasoning audits.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose agent states and a partition-function framework for measuring post-training-induced structure, and report two Qwen3.5-9B task demonstrations.
sections.unique_caveat: Methodological boundary: the abstract reports two tasks on one model size/family; broader model and task generality is not established there.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 1.00, solely from 4 cross-lists (weighted component 1.00); no other positive signal is recorded for this candidate.

sections.title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI
sections.abstract: The paper replaces free-form LLM generation for natural-language-to-LTL translation with predefined-answer questions and a classifier, reporting comparable or better accuracy than local LLMs on three benchmarks at up to an order of magnitude lower runtime and energy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors formulate LTL translation as answering questions with predefined answers and use a System-One classifier; the abstract reports three-benchmark results and generalization to unseen propositions and temporal patterns.
sections.unique_caveat: Methodological boundary: the abstract reports three benchmarks but does not specify whether their hardware and operating conditions represent deployed robot constraints.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 1.00, solely from 4 cross-lists (weighted component 1.00); its cross-listing spans AI, language, logic, robotics, and systems.

sections.title: SecretAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Privacy Protection against Vision Language Models
sections.abstract: SecretAgent uses LLM agents to locate privacy-revealing visual evidence and iteratively adapt perturbations, with an appearance-review agent rejecting visible artifacts; the authors report tests across four privacy applications, five datasets, and six VLMs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce gradient-based and gradient-free multi-agent perturbation methods, claiming better image-fidelity/privacy tradeoffs and transfer to other VLMs in their reported evaluation.
sections.unique_caveat: Methodological boundary: the evidence in the abstract is limited to the stated four applications, five datasets, and six tested VLMs; performance outside those settings is not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 1.00, solely from 4 cross-lists (weighted component 1.00); its cross-listing spans CV, AI, security, learning, and multiagent systems.

sections.title: Perceive Once, Escalate on Demand: Handing Off Visual KV Memory from Small to Large VLMs
sections.abstract: Baton maps a small VLM's visual KV cache for use by a larger VLM during uncertain escalations, and the authors report matching re-watching to within about one point while using 28–47% less compute, with a larger per-escalation saving on 64-frame inputs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a per-layer linear map distilled without labels from the large model's answers, and report cascade results on RoboMME and zero-shot transfer to OpenEQA.
sections.unique_caveat: Methodological boundary: the abstract's evidence names RoboMME, OpenEQA, and eight model pairs from four families; it does not establish performance across all VLM architectures or embodied tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 1.00, solely from 4 cross-lists (weighted component 1.00); its cross-listing spans vision, language, learning, AI, and robotics.

sections.title: SLP-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Acoustic Claims of Reasoning Audio Language Models on Clinical Speech
sections.abstract: SLP-Bench evaluates whether acoustic claims in reasoning audio-language-model outputs agree with clinician ratings, and the authors report factuality, stability, and consistency results across five datasets and 25 perceptual dimensions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce claim-level clinician-grounded evaluation and report that GRPO fine-tuning raised claim balanced accuracy from 0.54 to 0.60 and mean kappa from 0.39 to 0.61, while preserving answer accuracy on per-dimension questions.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that SLP-Bench is available upon request and subject to approval by the providers of each dataset, which constrains immediate independent access.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 0.75, solely from 3 cross-lists (weighted component 0.75); its AI/language/learning cross-lists give broad relevance and the work directly evaluates model-generated reasoning claims.

sections.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
sections.abstract: Embodied-Harness uses an Actor and Reflector with hierarchical memory to refine reusable robot-execution guidance without updating model parameters; the authors report results on three benchmarks and three real-world manipulation tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose evidence-based reflection and recursive harness refinement; their abstract reports benchmark success rates of 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4%, plus a 96.7% average over three real-world tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: Methodological boundary: real-world results cover three manipulation tasks; durability and transfer across broader robot platforms or environments are not established in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 0.75, solely from 3 cross-lists (weighted component 0.75); Semantic Scholar recorded 0 citations and 0 influential citations at collection time. Robotics/AI/vision/multiagent breadth and reported real-world evaluation support relevance, not measured popularity.

sections.title: PaMuk-Bench: A Parallel Multilingual Multitask Benchmark for Vision-Language Tasks
sections.abstract: PaMuk-Bench provides over 10,000 English prompts translated into Arabic, Danish, French, Hindi, Italian, and Romanian for five vision-language tasks, with parallel text and generated or retrieved images.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a parallel multilingual, multitask VLM benchmark and report that zero-shot English and multilingual pretrained models perform worse than fine-tuned counterparts in their experiments.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors describe translations as semi-automatic and cover six languages; translation quality and conclusions for languages outside that set remain open questions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 0.75, solely from 3 cross-lists (weighted component 0.75); its vision/language/learning/AI breadth and multilingual evaluation focus make it a relevant benchmark contribution in this batch.

sections.title: Run One, Get Two: Near-Free Streaming Safety Checks for Local LLMs
sections.abstract: ToRA adds a second model as an extra decoding row that shares the generator's weights and KV cache; the authors report under 4% added per-token latency on Qwen3-0.6B while improving on a hidden-state safety probe.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose dual-row decode kernels that share weight reads and KV cache; on Qwen3-0.6B they report higher F1 than a dedicated guard on 12 of 17 benchmarks and 11.8 points more unsafe-response detection than the probe at similar cost.
sections.unique_caveat: Methodological boundary: the abstract reports evaluation on Qwen3-0.6B; results on larger or different local model families are not established there.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 0.75, solely from 3 cross-lists (weighted component 0.75); Semantic Scholar recorded 0 citations and 0 influential citations at collection time. No matched external attention was found.

items.theme: Agent behavior is being made measurable and reusable
items.summary: The selected work models agent states, reuses robot-execution evidence, and adapts privacy perturbations through multi-agent loops; these are distinct approaches, not one established architecture.
Structured classification for LTL, visual KV-memory handoff, and shared decoding weights/cache target runtime or compute costs, with task- and model-bounded evaluations.
Clinical-audio claim validation and parallel multilingual VLM benchmarking emphasize evidence quality and language coverage.
Privacy protection with image fidelity and streaming safety with low incremental latency make tradeoffs explicit, without establishing deployment-wide safety.
The eight selected papers have primary categories cs.AI (3), cs.CV (3), cs.LG (1), and cs.RO (1); this is not a count of the full candidate pool.

items.text: Song and Zhu demonstrate their framework on two tasks with Qwen3.5-9B. Test replication across model families, task types, and independently specified state representations.

Schön et al. report three benchmarks and generalization to unseen propositions and temporal patterns. Evaluate ambiguous or adversarial instructions and end-to-end correctness/resource use on target robot hardware.
Test SecretAgent against adaptive attackers and image transformations such as compression or resizing, measuring privacy leakage alongside downstream image utility.
Test Baton cache maps and escalation thresholds under distribution shift, longer histories, and varied hardware budgets, including cases where the small model omits critical evidence.

SLP-Bench is available upon request and subject to dataset-provider approval. A reproducibility path using shareable data and stratified audits across accents and recording conditions could separate model failures from dataset effects.
Longer repeated robot trials could test whether Embodied-Harness reflections remain safe, improve rather than overfit, and transfer between embodiments.

PaMuk-Bench uses semi-automatically translated prompts in six languages. Human translation validation and expansion to additional low-resource languages and scripts would test translation artifacts versus model capability.
Profile ToRA accuracy/latency across model sizes and hardware and test shared decoding under longer contexts and varied unsafe-content distributions.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: This batch emphasizes making agentic and multimodal AI cheaper to run, easier to audit, or safer without sacrificing usability. The ordering is weak as a popularity ranking because scores are driven by cross-list breadth, not observed attention; the most defensible takeaway is the concrete evaluation and systems work exposed by these preprints.

sections.title: Method and sources
sections.method: Scores among selected entries were cross-list only: four cross-lists gave 1.00; three gave 0.75. Two selected records had Semantic Scholar totals of zero citations and zero influential citations; missing candidate-level records were not interpreted as zero. All eight arXiv abstract pages were verified. PDF text inspection for the top three could not be completed because a local PDF text extractor was unavailable, so contribution and caveat claims remain abstract-grounded.
